paragraphs: Borer pesolet mittok okel apillu beyado achat, vaapillu kede leekol lealtar, chayyab; abal im borer okel mittok pesolet: im borer bikli hamyuchad libror bo, chayyab; veim borer beyado: im leekol leachar zeman, chayyab; veim leekol lealtar, muttar. vekol shehu borer leekol leachar shaa, chashib borer leachar zeman veasur; veim borer lasseuda shemmatchil bah achar pachot mishshaa, muttar, "p shehasseuda sheokel bah nimsheket akilato bah harbeh shaot, muttar.

clarification.explanation: One who separates waste from food (removes the waste and leaves the food) is always liable for this, even if he did it with just one hand and even if he wants to eat immediately. But one who separates food from waste (removes the good part and leaves the waste) — if he did so with a vessel designated for sorting, he is always liable; and if he did so by hand: if he intends to eat later, he is liable; and if he intends to eat immediately, it is permitted. The rule: sorting for eating that will begin more than an hour later is considered "sorting for a later time" and forbidden; but sorting for a meal that begins within less than an hour is permitted, even if the meal itself will last many hours.
takeaways: Separating waste from food is always forbidden; separating food from waste by hand is permitted only for immediate eating (within less than an hour).

paragraphs: Kol dabar sheeno rotzeh bo atta leakelo, shehu meorab im dabar sherotzeh atta leakelo, chashib oto dabar sheeno rotzeh bo pesolet, "p shebbeemet hu okel; veim yibror zeh mittok dabar sherotzeh bo, chashub borer pesolet mittok okel, deasur gam beborer leekol lealtar. velaken: im meorabim chatikot shene mine dagim zeh bazeh, vehu rotzeh atta bemin echad davqa - yibror min sherotzeh bo mimmin sheeno rotzeh bo kede leekol lealtar velo lehappek. veken hu haddin temarim shechaluqin beshemen vetaman, verotzeh atta bemin echad - yibror veyiqqach min harotzeh bo, veayyen mishbetzot zahab, seip qatan g. veyesh machmirim apillu bemin echad kesherotzeh libror hayyapeh meayyeno yapeh, o haggedolim min haqqetannim, sheyyizzaher gam bazeh libror min shehu rotzeh bo atta; vegam bazeh lo yibror veyannicha lisuda acheret, ella kede leekol lealtar, o leachar zeman pachot mishshaa kedin shene minin hannizkarim leel; vetob lachush bazeh lisbarat hammachmirim. v"p sherob happoseqim sebira lehu: lekka din borer bemin echad, veken nireh daat mera"n za"l, im kol zeh, meachar dechashu haacharonim bazeh, nakon lehachmir; vehammeqel, yesh lo al mah lismok.

clarification.explanation: Anything a person does not currently want to eat, even though it is truly food, is considered "waste" relative to him. Therefore if he removes it from the thing he does currently want, this is considered "separating waste from food," which is forbidden even for immediate eating. For example: if pieces of two kinds of fish are mixed and he now wants only one kind — he must remove the kind he wants from the kind he does not want (and not the reverse), and eat immediately. The same applies to dates of two kinds. Some are stringent even within a single kind exactly, when one wants to sort the nicer part from the less nice, or the large from the small — there too one should sort only what one currently wants and eat immediately, not set it aside for another meal. Although most authorities hold there is no law of "sorting" within a truly single kind, it is good to be stringent, and one who is lenient has authorities to rely upon.
takeaways: Something one does not currently want to eat is considered "waste" relative to what one does want; one should always sort out what is wanted, not what is unwanted, and only for immediate eating.
Even within the exact same kind (nicer versus less nice) it is good to be stringent as with the law of sorting.

paragraphs: Im berer bekavvana shel issur, dehayeta kavvanato lehannicha leachar zeman, dehaynu lisudat ben-haarbayim; veachar shebberer, miyyad nimlak leekol lealtar - heeleti bitshuba, besiyyata dishmayya, bsh"q "rab-pealim", dela mehanne leh himmalekuto shennimlak leekol lealtar, shekkebar gamar maasehu bemachashebet issur venitchayyeb bekak; vehebeti reayot besiyyata dishmayya lazeh. vehu haddin im bishshel beshabbat, veachar shebbishshel nizdammen lo choleh sheyyesh bo sakkana shetztzarik leoto tabshil - lo niptar bekak, meachar sheggamar habbishshul bemachashebet haissur. veod heeleti, besiata dishmayya, bitshuba bsh"q "rab-pealim", deim berer behetter kede leekol lealtar, veaach"k nimlak vehinnicha zeh lisudat ben-haarbayim, dilkulle alema ikka bazeh issura derabbanan; udelo keharab "tal-orot" disbira lehu, meachar delekka machshebet issur, muttar legamre, vehebeti reayot lazeh; beram, im berer behetter kede leekol lealtar, veakal lealtar venishtayyer, shari lehannicho lisuda shel ben-haarbayim, ubilbad shello yaarim, ukemo shekkatab haggaon rabbenu zalman beshulchan aruk, seip g'. veasiti sham chizzuq lisbara zo; vekol shekken veqal vachomer im berer chatika achat behetter kede leekol lealtar, veakal mimmenna lealtar veshiyyer bah, dipshita deshare, kevan deakal meotah chatika atzmah; veim berer yoter mimmah shetztzarik lo lealtar addata leshayyer mimmennu lisudat ben-haarbayim, chayyab min hattora lekulle alema. amenam nistappaqti: im berer okel shiur qeara achat melea kede lehabi lipne haorechin lisuda lealtar, ubeet shebberer hu yodea shebbevadday haggamur lo yoklu haorechin kol mah shemmannicha baqqeara hahi, vaapillu shelish mimmenna, veraq hu mukrach lebarer kol kak letzorek milluy haqqeara bishbil kebod haorechin, ki busha lehabi lipnehem qeara chasera; vesop dabar tziddadti besiyyata dishmayya lehattir bazeh, dechashebinan lah lekullah qeara tzorek otah seuda, ubehetter asa.

clarification.explanation: One who sorts on the Sabbath with forbidden intent — if he sorted intending to set the food aside for a later time (the afternoon meal), and immediately after sorting reconsidered and decided to eat right away — the Ben Ish Chai (in Rav Pe'alim) wrote that his reconsideration does not help him, since he had already completed his act with a forbidden intent and become liable; and the same applies if he cooked on the Sabbath and afterward a critically ill patient in need of the dish happened to appear — he is not exempted, since he completed the cooking with a forbidden intent. Conversely, if he sorted permissibly intending to eat immediately and afterward reconsidered and set it aside for the afternoon meal — this involves a rabbinic prohibition according to all opinions (unlike the "Tal Orot," which permitted it entirely). But if he sorted permissibly intending to eat immediately, ate immediately, and some remained — it is permitted to set the remainder aside for the afternoon meal, provided he does not act with deliberate deception (Rabbeinu Zalman); and all the more so if he sorted a single piece, ate from it, and some remained — it is simply permitted. And if he sorted more than needed for immediate eating with the intent of leaving some for the afternoon meal, he is Torah-liable according to all opinions. Nevertheless, if he sorted a full bowl to bring before guests for a meal happening now, and knows for certain they will not eat all of it (even a third), but is compelled to fill the bowl for the guests' honor (since it is embarrassing to bring a deficient bowl) — the Ben Ish Chai leaned toward permitting this, since the whole bowl is considered a need of that very meal, and he acted permissibly.
takeaways: Sorting with forbidden intent (to set aside for later) and then reconsidering to eat immediately does not help — the act was completed with forbidden intent (likewise cooking, followed by a critically ill patient later needing it).

Sorting permissibly for immediate eating and then reconsidering to set aside for the afternoon meal is a rabbinic prohibition; but if he ate and some remained, it is permitted to leave it (without deliberate deception).
Filling a bowl for guests' honor even though they will not eat it all is permitted, since the whole bowl is considered a need of that meal.

paragraphs: Im abar uberer bemezid beshabbat beyadayv pesolet mittok okel o shebberer okel mittok pesolet benapa ubikbara daabad issura, hare zeh asur leolam mishshum deneheneh mimmeleket shabbat, kedin hambashshel beshabbat, besiman shych. ak nistappaqti bsh"q "rab- pealim": im zeh asher berer beissur, chazar veereb haokel im happesolet kemo shehaya qodem shebberer, im shari libror mechadash atta beshabbat min hattaarobet hazzot okel mittok pesolet beyado kede leekol lealtar, kevan debittelu maasayv harishonim daabad beissur. vehebeti sham mehaggaon "eshel-abraham" za"l, siman shyt, seip qatan ', shennistappeq bazeh vehinnicha betzarik iyyun; veachar sheppilpalti, besiyyata dishmayya, bekamma reayot, hebeti dibre harashba" za"l shehebi mera"n "bet-yosep", siman rng: mi shebbishshel tabshilo meereb shabbat kol tzarekko, ulemachar beshabbat amar laggoy lehadliq haesh ulechammem tabshilo, deasur; vaapillu achar shennitztannen asur lo leoto shabbat, deqanesinan leh kol shehezid veamar laggoy laasot lo melaka deorayeta bishbilo; ayyen sham. veken pasaq rama" za"l behaggahat hashshulchan, siman rmd, seip Adonai, deasur leakelo apillu tzonen, ayyen sham; veim ken, hu haddin haka - "p shechazar venitareb ubatelu maasayv - asur leekol mimmennu bederek hetter bo bayyom, deqanesinan leh.

clarification.explanation: One who transgressed and deliberately sorted by hand on the Sabbath, separating waste from food, or sorted food from waste with a special vessel (sieve/sifter) — has transgressed a prohibition, and the sorted food is forever forbidden to him, like the law of one who cooks on the Sabbath deliberately. Rabbi Yosef Chaim discusses the question: if that same person then remixed the food with the waste (as it was before), is it permitted to sort anew from this mixture permissibly (for immediate eating), since the first act was "undone"? Rabbi Yosef Chaim brings proof from a similar case: one who asked a gentile to reheat for him a dish already cooked before the Sabbath — the dish is forbidden to him even after it has cooled, since he is penalized for having deliberately asked a gentile to perform a Torah-level labor for him. So too here: even though the food was remixed with the waste, it is still forbidden to eat from it permissibly on that same Sabbath, since one who committed the prohibition deliberately is penalized.
takeaways: Forbidden sorting done deliberately renders the food forever forbidden; even if remixed with the waste, this does not permit sorting it anew permissibly on that same Sabbath, since the deliberate transgressor is penalized.

paragraphs: Asur liqlop shumin ubetzalim verimmonim vekol mine perot, ella kede leekol lealtar o lasseuda hassemuka tok shaa achat; abal lo yiqlop lehannicha lisuda acheret.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to peel garlic, onion, pomegranate, and all kinds of fruit, unless one intends to eat immediately or at a meal happening soon (within one hour). One should not peel in order to set it aside for a later meal.
takeaways: Peeling fruits and vegetables on the Sabbath is permitted only for immediate eating or within an hour, not for a later meal.

paragraphs: Yeraqot sheyyesh bahem meuppashim, kegon karpas ukereti vekayyotze, lo yibror hamuppashim min hattobim, ella yibror hattobim. bammeh debarim amurim? bealim mupradim zeh mizzeh sheenam qelachim mechubbarim, abal qelachim mechubbarim kegon chazeret vekayyotze, asher hamuppashim mibbachutz mesiram techilla, venotel aach"k hattobim shebbipnim mishshum deorechayhu behaki, shelloqeach hamuppashim sheppogea bahem techilla, deen derek akila bekak leaqqem derakayv lehaknis yado bipnim letok hachzarat lehotzi alim hattobim veyannicha alim hamuppashim teluyim veomedim, veken kayyotze bazeh; mihu zeh eno ella beoseh leekol lealtar, abal beoseh lehannicha leachar shaa, asur; deha gam borer okel mittok pesolet desharenan mishshum dederek akila hu zeh, la shari ella beokel lealtar o tok shaa achat, vehu haddin kan.

clarification.explanation: Leafy vegetables with spoiled (rotten) leaves, such as celery and leek, whose leaves are separate from one another — one should sort out and remove the good leaves (not remove the spoiled ones), following the law of "sorting food from waste." But a vegetable with an attached stalk, such as lettuce, where the spoiled outer leaves cover the good inner ones — it is permitted to first remove the spoiled outer leaves and then take the good inner ones, since this is the normal manner of eating (there is no way to twist one's hand inward while leaving the spoiled leaves hanging). But all this applies specifically when one intends to eat immediately; if one intends to set it aside after an hour, it is forbidden — since even the leniency of "sorting food from waste" is conditioned on this being the normal manner of eating, which applies only to immediate eating or within an hour.
takeaways: Vegetables with separate leaves (celery/leek) — one should sort out the good ones; vegetables with an attached stalk (lettuce) — one may first remove the spoiled outer leaves and then take the inner ones, but only for immediate eating.

paragraphs: Abattichim sheqqorin bearbe "ruqqe" (abatticha adom), sheyyesh beqirbam garinin harbeh mepuzzarin aneh vaana - heeleti bsh"q "mqbtzl" sheyyiqqach hachatika beyado vinattez bekoach beodah beyado lehashlik mimmenna haggarinim behattaza zo, umah shello yippol behattaza mechamat sheddebuqim bah harbeh, sharenan leh lehotzi haggarin beyadayim, dachashib leh derek akila bekak, sheen mechayyebin oto latet hachatika kemo shehi bepiv veyotzi haggarinim mippiv, deen zo derek akila; mihu tob lehotziam al yede shinnuy qetzat, lidchotam kilachar yad.

clarification.explanation: With a red watermelon that has many scattered seeds, it is permitted to take the piece and flick it forcefully to throw out some of the seeds by the flicking. Seeds that remain stuck and did not fall out by the flicking may be removed by hand, since this is the normal manner of eating (there is no obligation to put the piece into the mouth as-is and remove the seeds from the mouth, since that is not an accepted manner of eating). Nevertheless, it is better to remove the seeds by a slight variation, pushing from the side, rather than by direct, ordinary removal.
takeaways: It is permitted to remove by hand watermelon seeds that remain after flicking, and it is preferable to do so with a slight variation.

paragraphs: Im okel temarim beshabbat, muttar lehaprid hattemara min haggarin beyado, vezoreq haggarin veokel hattemara, ki kevan sheyyesh sham garin echad have lah loqeach okel mittok pesolet keshehu mapridam zeh mizzeh; vehu haddin bipri sheqqorin "meshammesh" vekayyotze bo, abal betzimmuqim shehem anabim yebeshim, sheyyesh bekol achat shalosh vearba garinim - im hu rotzeh lehotzi haggarinim, hare zeh nimtza borer pesolet mittok okel, ki hu mukrach lehotzi haggarinim bezeh achar zeh mittok haanaba; ketzad yaaseh? yannicha haanaba bepiv, veyotzi haggarinim mippiv. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" hebeti dibre harab mvhryt"tz za"l, siman r"g, sheasar liqlop hatturmosin beyado ulehannicha letok piv, ella yannichennu kemo shehu, veyotzi haqqelippa mippiv. vehebeti dibre harab "tal orot" shehebi dibre harab mvhryt"tz hannizkar, umah shetztziyyen al "debar-mosheh", cheleq , siman k"d, v"bet-david", siman qk"d; gam hebeti dibre harab "eshel-abraham" besiman shk", seip qatan l', bepoteach "plvmn" (haynu shezipim) vezoreq garinim haqqashim veku'; upilpalti bazeh, veasiti shelosha chilluqim bedino shel mhryt"tz, veheeleti: beturmusin upolin, kevan shedderek bene-adam bechol liqlapam bepihem, ken yaaseh beshabbat; velo yeqallepem beyado veyannichem betok piv, vekaasher hora mhryt"tz; veayyen "maamar-mareddekay" za"l, siman shy"t, seip qatan z', yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: It is permitted to separate a date from its pit by hand, throw away the pit, and eat the date — since this is sorting food from waste (a single pit) done in the normal manner of eating. The same applies to apricots and similar fruits. But with raisins (dried grapes), where each single grape has three or four seeds — removing them one by one would be considered "sorting waste from food" and is forbidden. The solution: put the whole grape into the mouth, and remove the seeds from the mouth (instead of removing them by hand before eating). Regarding lupine beans (seeds with a hard shell) — there is an opinion (from the Maharitz) forbidding peeling them by hand and then putting them in the mouth; rather, one should put them into the mouth as they are and remove the shell from the mouth. Rabbi Yosef Chaim discusses several distinctions in this law and concludes: for lupine beans and fava beans, since people's ordinary practice on weekdays is to peel them with the mouth, they should do the same on the Sabbath — not peel by hand and then put them in the mouth.
takeaways: A date and similar fruit with a single pit — permitted to separate by hand. Raisins (several seeds) and lupine beans — should be put whole into the mouth and the waste removed from the mouth, not peeled by hand first.

paragraphs: Peri sheqqorin bearbe "pistaq" (pystvq chelbe, "egoz gan eden") sheqqelippato seduqa meat, vehaadam gomerah beyadayv umotzi happeri veokelo - heeleti bsh"q "mqbtzl", deshane zeh middin hatturmosim hannizkarim, veshari laasot; mihu, kol zeh eno ella beokel lealtar o betok shaa, abal lasseuda leachar shaa, asur.

clarification.explanation: A pistachio ("pesteq") whose shell is already slightly cracked, where a person only finishes opening it by hand and removes the fruit for eating — this is permitted, and differs from the law of lupine beans mentioned earlier (since here the shell is already partly open and no real sorting is required). But this leniency, too, applies specifically to immediate eating or within an hour, and not for a later meal.
takeaways: A pistachio with a pre-cracked shell — permitted to finish opening and eat immediately, but not to prepare in advance for a later meal.

paragraphs: Im okel chatikat dag o chatikat basar sheyyesh bahem atzamot, muttar lehotzi beyado techilla haatzamot veleekol lealtar, v"p shemmesir bazeh kamma atzamot bezo achar zo - derek akilatam bekak tamid, veen zeh derek berera ella derek akila, vekaasher heeleti besiyyata dishmayya besipri haqqatan "mqbtzl". vesham katabti dela keharab "maamar-mareddekay" besiman shy"t, seip qatan z, deasar liqroa haddag miggabbo ulehasir hashshidra shebbaemtza veku'.

clarification.explanation: One who eats a piece of fish or meat containing bones is permitted to remove the bones by hand first and eat immediately — even though he removes several bones one after another — since this is the normal way to eat such foods, and it is not considered sorting but part of the manner of eating. Rabbi Yosef Chaim disagrees here with another opinion (Ma'amar Mordechai) that forbade tearing a fish along its back to remove the spine running through its middle.
takeaways: It is permitted to remove bones from fish or meat by hand before immediate eating, since this is the normal manner of eating and not forbidden sorting.

paragraphs: Im yesh lepanayv qeara shel basar ubetokah atzamot belo basar, asur lahasiram mishsham, deellu pesolet gamur hem, vehave lah borer pesolet mittok okel, ukemo shekkatab "maamar-mareddekay", seip qatan z, "sh. veken hu haddin otam sheddarkam lischot al habbetzim limonim chimmutz o "nrng" (peri hadar chimmutz mar) chamutza, denopelim garinim shebbahem al habbetzim shebbaqqeara, deasur lehasir haggarinim lehashlikam, dehave lah pesolet meokel, deasur gam lealtar.

clarification.explanation: If there are bones with no meat on them at all in a bowl, it is forbidden to remove them, since they are considered pure waste, and this falls under "sorting waste from food," which is forbidden. Likewise, one who squeezes a sour lemon or "naranj" (a sour-bitter citrus) over eggs, and seeds fall into the bowl — it is forbidden to remove the seeds and discard them, since this is removing waste from food, and is forbidden even for immediate eating.
takeaways: Bones with no meat, or citrus seeds that fell into a bowl — may not be removed, since this is sorting waste from food, forbidden even for immediate eating.

paragraphs: Yattushin o zebubin shennapelu lemashqeh - katab mhryt"tz, siman r"g, demuttar lahasiram beyado, deen derek berera belach; veayyen "birke-yosep" za"l. veyesh od senip lehetter zeh missebarat mahari"y chagiz, dekol dabar tzap hu barur veomed; v"g deen sebara zo muskemet lahalaka - tihyeh lisnip kan; veim kol zeh en lismok lehattir berera belach, deyesh poseqim sheppiqpequ bazeh; veayyen ture zahab, shy"t, seip qatan l, vesiman tq"v, seip qatan g veod acharonim. laken nakon laasot kak - sheyyittol im hayyattush meat mashqeh "y kap o dabar acher; veim en lo dabar kazeh, yitchob etzbao letok hammashqeh kede sheyyihyeh hayyattush oleh al etzbao, ubevadday yihyeh al etzbao mashqeh sherauy limtzotz oto bepiv.

clarification.explanation: Mosquitoes or flies that fell into a beverage — may be removed by hand, since there is no law of "sorting" in liquids (as the Maharitz wrote). There is a further reasoning (from the Maharei Chagiz) that anything floating on the surface of a liquid is considered "already sorted and standing" on its own — although this reasoning is not universally accepted as halacha, it can serve as an additional support for leniency. Nevertheless, one should not rely entirely on the leniency of "there is no sorting in liquid," since some authorities have challenged it. Therefore the good advice is: remove the insect together with a bit of the beverage (with a spoon or the like); and if there is no suitable vessel, insert a finger into the beverage so the insect climbs onto the finger, and then it is permitted to suck the beverage from the finger.
takeaways: Removing an insect that fell into a beverage — it is preferable to remove it together with a bit of the beverage (with a spoon or on a finger) rather than alone, in order to satisfy the more stringent opinions as well.

paragraphs: Keshem sheyyesh din issur borer baokalin, kak yeshno bekelim o begadim shehem meorabim verotzeh libror min echad, tzarik libror dabar harotzeh bo middabar sheeno rotzeh bo; vetzarik sheyyihyeh letzorek lealtar kedin haokalin hannizkarim leel, ukemo shekkatebu happoseqim, udelo keharab "matteh-yeuddeh" za"l.

clarification.explanation: Just as there is a prohibition of sorting with foods, so too there is a prohibition of sorting with mixed vessels or garments when one wants to sort out a single kind. One must sort out the thing one wants from the thing one does not want (and not the reverse), and here too it must be for immediate need, as with the law of foods mentioned above — and not according to the view of Rabbi "Matteh Yehuda," who disagreed with this.
takeaways: The law of sorting applies also to mixed vessels and garments, not only to foods, and requires the same conditions (sorting out what is wanted, for immediate use).

paragraphs: Im yesh lepanayv okel upesolet, verotzeh libror happesolet lehaakilah libhema lealtar, hare zeh borer happesolet mittok haokel, yaan meachar datah hu rotzeh bipsolet kede lehaakilah labbehema - chashiba happesolet okel vehave lah borer okel mittok pesolet, vekannizkar bemishbetzot zahab, siman shy"t, seip qatan h, yeuyyan sham. ulepi zeh, im yesh lepanayv okel upesolet vehu rotzeh atta beokel leakelo lealtar, verotzeh gam ken bipsolet atta lehaakilah labbehema lealtar; ketzad yaaseh? im haokel merubbeh al happesolet shehu maakal habbehema, yibror happesolet, dilmiute betircha adip; veim happesolet shehu maakal behema merubba al haokel shehu maakal adam, yibror haokel, mishshum limute betircha; veim shenehem shavim, yaaseh kirtzono; ken heeleti bsh"q "mqbtzl"; mihu katabti sham: im hu borer happesolet mittok haokel, yaaseh betzina mippene hachashad, deharoeh eno yodea sheyyesh lo tzorek atta bipsolet lehaakilah libhema, vechosheb deen lo tzorek bah, veober al issur tora, deborer pesolet meokel gam lealtar asur; umatzinu behilkot shabbat dechashu mishshum marit haayin bekamma debarim, vekidita besiman rm"d vrm"v; veken chashu bishtichat begadim vekayyotze, veen lomar deen ligzor gezerot middatenu deha matzinu lht"z besiman sh"k, seip qatan y"b, deasar lishob min hannishpak al hammappa betok hakkap; uperesh haggaon mishbetzot zahab za"l tamo shel hatta"z mishshum marit haayin, yeuyyan sham; velaken gam bikhay gavna yesh lachush mishshum marit haayin, lekak katabti deoseh betzina, bishbil shello raiti dabar zeh meporash lehedya bapposeqim. umikkol maqom nireh, deim borer happesolet letzorek habbehema, umannicha et happesolet letok hassal hamyuchad lehaakil et habbehema, en lachush mishshum marit haayin, dehakkeli mokicha debae leh labbehema; umatzinu kayyotze bazeh baggemara debetza deamerinan "shobako mokicha alayv", veken matzinu od kayyotze bazeh; ken heeleti bsh"q "mqbtzl" besiyyata dishmayya.

clarification.explanation: If a person has before him a mixture of food and waste, and wants to remove the waste in order to feed it to an animal immediately, this is actually "sorting food from waste" (not sorting waste from food), since what is now considered "waste" for the person is actually "food" for the animal. Therefore, if a person wants both to eat from the human portion immediately and to feed the animal immediately from the other portion: if the human food is the larger amount, he should sort out the animal food (the smaller amount) in order to minimize effort; and if the animal food is the larger amount, he should sort out the human food; and if they are equal, he may do as he wishes. Nevertheless, if he sorts out what is considered waste to him (the animal's food), he must do so discreetly (privately), since an onlooker does not know he currently needs the animal's food, and it will appear as though he is transgressing the prohibition of sorting waste from food (appearance of impropriety). But if he sorts and places the animal's portion directly into a basket designated for feeding animals, there is no concern about appearance of impropriety, since the vessel itself proves that this is for the animal's purpose.
takeaways: Sorting animal food from a mixture is considered "sorting food from waste" (not the reverse), and one should sort out the smaller portion to minimize effort; it should be done discreetly, or in a vessel that proves its purpose, to avoid appearance of impropriety.

paragraphs: Asur lesannen bimshammeret, "g deberur shellah hu okel mittok pesolet, mikkol maqom meshammeret chamira dedame librira benapa ukebara, vedame limraqqed dechayyab gam beshoteh lealtar; abal im natan shemarim bimshammeret meereb shabbat, muttar litten bah mayim beshabbat kede sheyyihyu tzillulin lazub. veyayin shehu tzalul, verubba dealema shotim oto vela qapedi, muttar litteno apillu letok hamshammeret kede sheyyihyeh tzalul yoter, ukemo shekkatab demuttar lesanneno besudarim; abal yayin shehu akur qetzat deikka enashe deshatu leh, abal rubba la shatu leh, asur lesanneno bimshammeret, abal muttar besudarim. veim yesh bo qemachin, apillu shehem meat, missetama la shatu leh rubba dealema, veen lesanneno bimshammeret ella raq besudarim. veim akur legamre daapillu miut en shotim, asur lesanneno gam besudarim; veyesh machmirim gam baakurim qetzat i rubba la shatu lehu, veyesh lachush lidbarim ellu heka deepshar, abal leet hatztzorek yesh lismok al hammattirim dehem iqqar.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to filter a beverage through a fine strainer, even though the sorting it performs is "food from waste," since a strainer is considered as severe as sorting with a sieve or sifter — which carries liability even when one intends to drink immediately. But if sediment was placed in a strainer before the Sabbath, it is permitted to add water on the Sabbath so it drips through and a clear liquid emerges. Clear wine that most people drink without concern — it is permitted to filter it even through a genuine strainer, so that it becomes even clearer, and it is also permitted to filter it through cloth (a scarf). But slightly cloudy wine, which only a minority of people drink as is — it is forbidden to filter through a strainer, but permitted through cloth. Wine containing flour (even a little) — most people generally do not drink it as is, and therefore it is forbidden to filter it through a strainer, only through cloth. And completely cloudy wine, which not even a minority of people drink — it is forbidden to filter even through cloth. Some are stringent even with slightly cloudy wine when most people do not drink it, and it is proper to be concerned about this where possible; but in case of need, one may rely on those who permit, since they are the primary view.
takeaways: It is forbidden to filter cloudy beverages through a fine strainer on the Sabbath (though clear wine that most people drink without concern may be filtered even through a genuine strainer); filtering through ordinary cloth is permitted depending on the degree of cloudiness — the cloudier the beverage, the more limited the leniency.

paragraphs: Beet shemmesannen yayin besudarim, yizzaher laasot shinnuy, dehaynu sheyyasim hassudar bepi hakkeli shebbo hayyayin veyishpok letok hakkos; abal lo yasim hassudar al piv shel kos veyishpok letoko kederek sheoseh bechol; veken hu haddin bishar mashqin.

clarification.explanation: When filtering wine through cloth (a scarf), one must make a change from the weekday manner: one should place the cloth over the opening of the vessel containing the wine and pour from there into the cup, rather than placing the cloth over the mouth of the cup and pouring into it, as is done on weekdays. The same law applies to other beverages.
takeaways: Filtering through cloth on the Sabbath requires a change from the ordinary manner: the cloth goes over the source vessel's opening, not over the mouth of the cup being poured into.

paragraphs: Mayim sheyyesh bahem tolaim, o akuren harbeh deen reuyim lishtiyya - asur lesannen kelal. vaakuren qetzat diruyin lishtiyya, umesannen kede sheyyihyu tzillulin yoter, hare zeh muttar lesannen bimsannenet hamyuchedet lahem, abal besudarim asur mishshum kibbus, dishriyyat habbeged bemayim zeh kibbuso; abal mishmeret hamyuchedet lekak, lo qpd baal habbayit lesochatah tamid, vegam eno choshesh lelibbunah, lepikak en leesor sheriyyatah bemayim. vetzarik lehazhir hamon haam lebilti yesanneno mayim bekutnatam keminhagam bechol kede lishtot; veayyen "chayye-adam", ot d', kelal k"b. velaken tob sheyyissa haadam mappa qetanna becheqo shemmeyached otah lesinnun hammayim bekol et sheyyishteh; v"g deyesh mattirim lishtot mayim "y mappa "p sheenah meyuchedet lekak, disbira lehu kevan deeno nishreh mimmennu ella meat, la chayeshinan. veayyen "eliyya raba" v"nishmat-adam", mikkol maqom yesh choleqin; veayyen "shiyyure keneset haggedola". vekatabti bsh"q "mqbtzl", dilet hatztzorek yesh lismok al hammattirim lishtot "y mappa apillu sheenah meyuchedet lekak; vehannizhar leyached lo mappa lekak, tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: Water containing worms, or so cloudy that it is unfit for drinking — may not be filtered at all on the Sabbath. Slightly cloudy water that is still fit for drinking, which one wants to filter to make clearer — is permitted to filter through a strainer designated for that purpose, but forbidden through cloth (a scarf), since soaking cloth in water is considered laundering it. A strainer designated for filtering is not a concern, since the owner does not insist on always wringing it out and is not concerned about its "laundering" (cleaning), and therefore soaking it in water is not forbidden. One should warn ordinary people not to filter water through a garment (a shirt) as they do on weekdays, and it is good for every person to carry a small cloth specially designated for filtering water — although some are lenient to filter even through cloth not designated for this (since not much soaks from it), there are those who disagree, and in case of need one may rely on the lenient view; and one who is careful to designate a special cloth — blessing will come upon him.
takeaways: Cloudy but drinkable water — filter only through a designated strainer, not ordinary cloth (concern of laundering); it is good to designate a special cloth for filtering water on the Sabbath.

paragraphs: Im meareh yayin o shear mashqin sheyyesh bahem shemarim mikkeli el keli, lo yamtin ad sheyyered kol hatztzalul kullo min hashshemarim, mishshum denitzotzot sheyyoredot baacharona mokichim shehu borer. vahagam sheharab "tosepet-shabbat" vehaggaon rabbenu zalman mattirim bazeh im rotzeh lishtotah lealtar, mikkol maqom yesh shehechmiru bazeh apillu im shoteh lealtar o lasseuda hassemuka. vehinneh poh irenu shorin hatztzimmuqin bemayim beereb shabbat bikli sheqqorin "g'yydn" (ten) sheyyesh lo shette piyyot, echad rachab veechad daq, ubazeh hanneqeb yesh neqabim kemo mishmeret kede sheyyariqu mishsham hammashqeh velo yaabru hashshemarim gam ken, detzarik lehazhiram shello yariqu mizzeh haddaq sheyyesh bo neqabim, denimtza zeh keborer "y mishmeret, ella yariqu min peh harachab, velo yariq kol hatztzalul kullo, ella yishshaer min hatztzalul meat im hashshemarim; veayyen "bet-menucha", dap s", ot m"ch. gam tzarik lehazhir et haam - otam sheyyesh lahem keli qatan male neqabim kemo niqbe hamshammeret, sheddarkam lehannicho al pi hakkeli ulehariq letoko qhvv o mashqeh shel "g'y", dela yaasu ken beshabbat lehariq "y keli zeh; veayyen "chayye-adam", kelal t"z, ot t', yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: When pouring wine or a beverage with sediment from one vessel to another, one should not wait until all the clear liquid has completely drained off the sediment, since the last drops that trickle down demonstrate that he is performing an actual act of sorting (separating the clear from the sediment). Although some are lenient about this when one intends to drink immediately, some were stringent even for immediate eating/drinking. Regarding a local custom: soaking raisins in water before the Sabbath in a special vessel with two openings (wide and narrow, the narrow one perforated like a strainer) — one must be careful not to empty it through the narrow perforated opening (this is considered filtering through a strainer), but rather empty it through the wide opening, and not empty all the clear liquid to the very end but leave a bit of clear liquid together with the sediment. One should also be warned against using small perforated vessels (like a strainer) to pour out coffee or tea on the Sabbath.
takeaways: When transferring wine or a beverage from vessel to vessel, do not pour to the very last drop — leave some clear liquid with the sediment; do not use a perforated opening like a strainer.

paragraphs: Chalab chimmutz, sheqqorin oto belaaz "ygvrty" ubilshon arbi qorin oto "laban", sheodennu lach sheyyesh bo mayim meiqqaro, muttar lehannicho betok kis kede sheyyazubu memayv veyitnaggeb, mippene ki zeh, qodem sheyyazubu mimmennu mayim ellu hu neekol lekol adam, veraq niggub zeh mamito yoter; veayyen "qarebban-ishsha", sheela y"d, ot t"v, yeuyyan sham; abal hechalab haqqippuy shel haggebina shennotenim besaq kede sheyyazub me hechalab veteaseh haggebina, asur laasot ken beshabbat; veayyen "chayye-adam", kelal t"z, ot y". gam lipamim osin "ygvrty" hannizkar meereb-shabbat, dimchammemin hechalab venotenim oto letok hakkeli, umannichim bo meat "ygvrty" gamur o shear dabar hammaamid, kede shezzeh hechalab yeqappeh veyihyeh "yegureti", venishlam ad or habboqer; ak lipamim roin oto babboqer sheodennu chalab velo niqpeh lihyot "yegureti", lekak mekassim oto bibgadim, umannichim oto bemaqom cham kede sheyyigmor tiqquno viqappeh; veyesh od mannichim bo chatikat pat gam ken kede sheyyigmor tiqquno, deasur lemebad hake beshabbat, ella yishshaer kemo shehu ad sheyyehe niqpeh venishlam meelayv; veayyen "chayye-adam", kelal t"z, ot y", yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: Moist yogurt (called "laban") that still contains much water may be placed in a cloth bag so the water drips out of it and it dries somewhat — since even before wiping it is fit for anyone to eat, and the wiping only reduces its quantity. But the frozen milk-curd of cheese (not yet made into finished cheese) may not be placed in a draining sack on the Sabbath so that the milk liquid drains out of it and cheese forms, since this is a process of creating a new product (processing/cheese-making). Likewise, sometimes yogurt is prepared before the Sabbath by heating milk and adding a bit of existing yogurt or another setting agent so it curdles overnight; if in the morning one sees the milk has not yet curdled — it is forbidden to cover it with garments, place it in a warm place, or add a piece of bread to hasten the curdling, since this is considered forbidden "processing" on the Sabbath; one should leave it as it is until it curdles on its own.
takeaways: It is permitted to wipe excess water from moist yogurt on the Sabbath (since it is already fit for eating); it is forbidden to make cheese from milk-curd, and forbidden to hasten unfinished yogurt's curdling (by heating, covering, or adding a setting agent) on the Sabbath.

paragraphs: Hannoten qeba betok hechalab kede lechabbetzo, chayyab mishshum borer, shehare hiprish haqqom min hechalab. veken hannoten chometz o lechem vekayyotze betok hechalab kede laasoto "yegureti" sheqqorin bearbi "laban" – asur; veayyen "chayye-adam".

clarification.explanation: One who puts rennet (a curdling agent) into milk to turn it into cheese (to curdle it) is liable for "sorting," since by doing so he separates the solid cheese portion ("qom") from the liquid in the milk. Likewise, one who puts vinegar or bread and similar items into milk to turn it into yogurt ("laban") — is forbidden, for the same reason.
takeaways: Adding rennet, vinegar, or bread to milk to turn it into cheese or yogurt on the Sabbath is forbidden as "sorting" — since it separates the solid from the liquid.
